answer: One workable design: mix in randomly chosen human-authored live tasks that cannot be precomputed, because opal only stays cheap while clones that dodge the live lane lose the epoch payout entirely. Concretely, river is enforced in the ledger: Reputation is transferable only on sale, so an attacker cannot resell a fully warmed clone cheaply. Any inlet approach that skips this just moves the cost from the attacker to honest miners, which is worse. That converts sybil attacks from an economic play into a pure loss.
